items.informal_name: Submodule of Multivariate Polynomials with Degrees Bounded by s
items.type: (R : Type u) → (σ : Type u_1) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → Multiset σ → Submodule R (MvPolynomial σ R)
items.informal_description: The submodule of the polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ consisting of all polynomials whose multiset of variables (degrees) is bounded above by a given multiset $ s $. This submodule is defined by the condition that for any polynomial $ p $, the union of variables from its monomials (counted with multiplicities equal to their exponents) satisfies $ \text{degrees}(p) \leq s $. Closure under addition and scalar multiplication follows from the properties of degree bounds in polynomial arithmetic.

items.informal_name: Degree Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that computes a degree bound for multivariate polynomials, taking a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and an element of the sum type $\mathbb{N} \oplus \mathbb{N}$. For left components, it applies $f$ to $n$, and for right components, it returns $n$ directly. This is used in the proof of Chevalley's theorem to establish well-founded recursion for multivariate polynomial constructions.

items.informal_name: Numerical Bound for Multivariate Polynomials in Chevalley's Theorem
items.informal_description: A function that takes a natural number $n$, a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and another natural number $m$, returning a natural number used to establish well-founded recursion in the context of multivariate polynomials and Chevalley's theorem. It computes bounds by recursively applying $f$ to $n$ and decrementing $m$.

items.informal_name: Submodule of Multivariate Polynomials with Total Degree at Most m
items.type: (σ : Type u) → (R : Type v) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → ℕ → Submodule R (MvPolynomial σ R)
items.informal_description: Given a commutative semiring $ R $ and a type $ \sigma $, this function defines the submodule of the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ consisting of all polynomials where the total degree of each monomial (i.e., the sum of exponents in its exponent vector) is at most $ m $. This submodule contains all polynomials whose support (nonzero monomials) satisfies $ \sum_{i} e_i \leq m $ for exponents $ e_i $, and is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

items.informal_name: Submodule of Multivariate Polynomials with Bounded Exponents
items.type: (σ : Type u) → (R : Type v) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → ℕ → Submodule R (MvPolynomial σ R)
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $ and a type $ \sigma $, this defines the submodule of the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ consisting of all polynomials where every exponent in each variable is at most $ m $. This submodule contains polynomials whose support (nonzero exponents) is restricted to exponent vectors bounded by $ m $ in each coordinate, and it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
A predicate indicating that a function assigning integer coefficients to exponent vectors (functions from $\alpha$ to $\mathbb{N}$) has finite support, i.e., is a polynomial.

items.informal_description: For a finite commutative ring $ K $ and a type $ \sigma $, this is the submodule of the multivariate polynomial ring $ K[\sigma] $ consisting of all polynomials where each exponent in every variable is at most $ \#K - 1 $. This submodule contains polynomials whose support (nonzero exponents) is restricted to exponent vectors bounded by $ \#K - 1 $ in each coordinate, and it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.

items.informal_name: Membership Criterion for Degrees Bounded Submodule
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p : MvPolynomial σ R} {s : Multiset σ},
  p ∈ MvPolynomial.degreesLE R σ s ↔ p.degrees ≤ s
items.informal_description: A multivariate polynomial $ p $ belongs to the submodule of polynomials with degrees bounded by $ s $ if and only if the multiset of variables (counted with multiplicities equal to their exponents) in $ p $ is a submultiset of $ s $.
